- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase early forecast values, especially if history shows downward trend.
- Model often overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 2024-05-08), producing exaggerated highs followed by sharp drops — cap forecast peaks at 2x recent high or 1.5x median of last 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust — force a gradual upward correction starting from day 10–15 of forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.5x median of 18-day history, reduce by 15–30% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- For 30d forecasts, avoid extreme low values (e.g., <0.5) when sentiment is positive — model often underestimates upside potential.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/0.67 alternation, model tends to oscillate — smooth forecast curve with exponential decay toward historical mean.
